guarantees.claim: rx_in_maj is the majority vote of rx_sync, rx_sync_q1, rx_sync_q2.
rx_in_mx is rx_in_maj when rxnf_enable is true, otherwise rx_sync.
rx_in is tx_out when sys_loopback is true, else 1'b1 when line_loopback is true, else rx_in_mx.

uart_rx is instantiated with rx input connected to rx_in, parity_enable and parity_odd to reg2hw control bits, tick_baud to rx_tick_baud, and its outputs rx_valid, rx_data, idle, frame_err, rx_parity_err connected to the corresponding signals.
rx_fifo_wvalid is asserted only when rx_valid is high and both event_rx_frame_err and event_rx_parity_err are low.

assumptions.claim: rx_sync, rx_sync_q1, rx_sync_q2 are synchronized, glitch-free versions of the external RX pin.
assumptions.cond: when used for majority vote (rxnf_enable active or normal operation)
assumptions.risk: Metastability in rx_sync could propagate through the majority filter, causing rx_in_maj to glitch and produce false rx data or spurious frame errors.

assumptions.claim: rxnf_enable, sys_loopback, line_loopback remain constant while rx_enable is active.
assumptions.cond: during active UART frame reception (rx_enable high)
assumptions.risk: Changing any of these controls mid‑frame could cause a glitch in rx_in, leading to corrupted receive data or spurious framing/parity errors.

assumptions.claim: Parity configuration bits reg2hw.ctrl.parity_en.q and reg2hw.ctrl.parity_odd.q are stable during a frame.
assumptions.cond: while uart_rx is receiving a frame (rx_valid active)
assumptions.risk: Inconsistent parity checking would cause false parity errors or, if parity is disabled mid‑frame, mask true parity errors, compromising data integrity.

assumptions.claim: rx_tick_baud is a clean, glitch‑free pulse aligned with the expected RX sampling point.
assumptions.risk: A glitchy rx_tick_baud would cause uart_rx to sample at wrong times, leading to data corruption.

uncertain_points.claim: rx_fifo_wvalid gates only event_rx_frame_err and event_rx_parity_err. If uart_rx provides additional error outputs (break, overrun, etc.) that indicate invalid data, they are not connected, potentially allowing erroneous data into the RX FIFO.
uncertain_points.cond: when uart_rx asserts an error other than frame or parity error
uncertain_points.risk: Corrupted or unwanted data may be written into the FIFO, propagating to software and breaking data integrity.

uncertain_points.claim: When both sys_loopback and line_loopback are asserted, rx_in receives tx_out (sys_loopback), ignoring the line_loopback idle value 1'b1. The specification may intend an error or an explicit priority, but the RTL silently prioritizes sys_loopback.
uncertain_points.risk: If software erroneously enables both, line_loopback behaviour is overridden, which may mask a software bug or test‑mode misuse. No functional hazard in itself.
